points.quote: The code is in `packages/frontend/core/src/modules/workbench`. ... `Workbench` (`entities/workbench.ts`) holds the list of open `View`s, the active view, a `basename`, and the right-sidebar state.
`View` (`entities/view.ts`) is one pane in the split-view layout. ... `open(to, options)` pushes or replaces a location on a view, and can open it in a new split view.
It also has a navigable memory history (`createNavigableHistory`) exposed as `location$` and `entries$`, with `push`, `replace` and `go(n)`
`ViewRoot` (`view/view-root.tsx`) creates a react-router `createMemoryRouter(routes)` for each view. A layout effect calls `router.navigate(location)` whenever `view.location$` changes.

A route component renders `<ViewHeader>`, `<ViewBody>` and `<ViewSidebarTab>` (`view/view-islands.tsx`). These are "islands": the content is portalled into targets placed by the workbench, which are looked up by view id.
The right sidebar (`view/sidebar/*`) shows the active view's sidebar tabs.

On web, `view/browser-adapter.ts` (`useBindWorkbenchToBrowserRouter`) keeps the active view's history and the browser's history in sync. ... If that location came from the view, the adapter instead finds the matching entry and calls `go(delta)`.
